ideas.title: I Raced AI Against Myself on a Boring Task
ideas.angle_hint: Short / Type A experiment (credibility): literal stopwatch race — me vs an AI on one real back-office task. Twist line (use verbatim): 'AI finished first… but that's not why it won.' The point isn't speed, it's that it runs unattended / never gets bored / doesn't fat-finger row 200. Predicted ~84. (Parked idea #2 from the counter-trend-money round.)
ideas.takeaway: Speed is the obvious win and the wrong one — the real value is that it runs unattended and never tires.

ideas.title: What My Automations Did Before I Finished My Coffee
ideas.angle_hint: Short / Type B-ish discovery (fast, visual, new-audience entry point — may out-view the credibility ones, so do NOT auto-rank it last). A tight before-coffee montage of small jobs already done by the time you sit down: rows filled, invoice chased, inbox triaged. Build as a visual discovery Short (optionally a light timed framing). Must differentiate from 003 (003 is the '5 secretary jobs' list; this is a single-morning montage, not a numbered list). Predicted ~80. (Parked idea #4 from the counter-trend-money round.)
ideas.takeaway: The payoff of boring automation is invisible: the work is just already done when you show up.

ideas.title: "Everyone Asks AI to X. I Asked It to Y." (repeatable Short series)
ideas.angle_hint: OWNER-ENDORSED REPEATABLE SHORT FORMAT (not a single idea): 'Everyone asks AI to [hyped thing]. I asked it to [boring back-office opposite]. Here's what happened.' Each entry rides a hyped search term, delivers our boring-automation angle, keeps the VISIBLE-PROOF beat (see proof-must-be-visible) + promise discipline (saves/keeps, never earns). 009 = make-money -> chase-invoices. Owner's other seeds: replace jobs -> replace copy-paste; write code -> clean spreadsheets. Pick the next one from these — but the picker must give it a fresh SUBJECT coordinate (subject-guard, D-059). RETIRED SEED (D-059, 2026-07-15): 'write emails -> find the emails I shouldn't answer' (015) was dropped as a near-duplicate of 011 (subject attention/inbox, already covered by 011 + 016); do NOT re-seed inbox triage here.
ideas.takeaway: Point AI at the boring opposite of the hype, and show the run — that's the recognizable format.

ideas.title: I Built an AI Employee. It Makes These Videos.
ideas.tool: Claude Code (agent) — our own studio pipeline
ideas.angle_hint: STUDIO REVEAL, anti-hype positioning (sequel to 010 point-of-trust). The channel's own autonomous studio as a public case-study: the system + review loops + QA + human gates + where it fails. Keep the searchable phrase 'AI employee' but with self-referential specificity; explicitly distance from the get-rich faceless genre (YouTube's July-2025 inauthentic-content policy punishes lazy mass automation — we position AS the counterexample: AI as production accelerator, human as creative direction + gates). Absorbs the 'Stop Building AI Agents Wrong' story (Input -> Validation -> Retries -> Human review). Message: leverage for a solo operator, not a magic worker.
ideas.takeaway: An 'AI employee' is leverage with human gates — validation, retries, review — not a magic worker you can walk away from.

Produce as a LONG only after the freelance cluster has lived; if a good incident lands earlier, a desk-notes Short is allowed immediately. Frame: failure-design (validation, alerts, fallbacks, human gates), not war stories.
ideas.takeaway: Every automation breaks eventually — the design goal is that it tells you, loudly, instead of failing silently.

ideas.title: The n8n Inbox That Triages Itself (and the One Node That Keeps It Safe)
ideas.tool: n8n (free, self-host) + Gmail + a modular classifier model
ideas.angle_hint: Teardown of a REAL public n8n template (workflow 4876) - understand WHY it works + the failure modes; label-only safety spine (a wrong guess = a wrong label, never a lost email). Bridges from the 015 Short. Establishes the reusable teardown FORMAT (ROADMAP Phase 3 #7).
ideas.takeaway: Automate the DECIDING (which emails need you), not the DOING; build it label-only so a misclassification is recoverable; the classifier is the fragile node - keep a human gate.

ideas.title: I Gave an AI Agent One Job: Watch the Fine Print
ideas.search_term: ai monitor terms of service changes
ideas.tool: AI agent (model-agnostic) + any change-watch source (a saved page / a doc / an RSS or diff feed); kept modular
ideas.angle_hint: Ep. 1 of 'The AI Agent'. An agent is a DECISION layer, not a scraper. A dumb diff-watcher spams you on every character change; the agent reads the change, decides whether it MATTERS, and hands you only the ones that do — with a reason. Money shot = a DECISION CARD (old vs new clause + AI verdict: impact + reason), not a scanning animation. Human-approval posture: it flags, you decide. subject = change-detection/policy; bridges to 016 (automate the deciding).
ideas.subject: change-detection/policy
ideas.takeaway: An AI agent isn't a scraper that flags every change — it's a decision layer that reads a change, judges whether it matters, and hands you the call. Automate the deciding, keep the approval.

ideas.title: AI Can't See the Letters in Your Words
ideas.search_term: what is a token in ai
ideas.subject: llm-mental-model
ideas.tool: None (concept video; tiktoken used only as the measuring instrument)
ideas.angle_hint: Not the definition ('~4 characters'). The letters never arrive — the model receives learned chunks, and the chunk is the only unit it perceives, remembers and bills.
ideas.takeaway: The chunk is the model's atom: it cannot look inside one, and it pays for every one. When an AI fails something trivially easy, ask what it can actually see — and put character-exact work in a tool, not in the guess.

ideas.title: AI Has No Memory — It Re-Reads Everything
ideas.search_term: what is a context window in ai
ideas.subject: llm-mental-model
ideas.tool: None (concept video; tiktoken used only as the measuring instrument, as in 021)
ideas.angle_hint: Not 'how much the AI remembers'. Nothing is remembered — every turn the whole conversation is handed back and re-read from scratch, and re-reading degrades with size and with position in the pile.
ideas.takeaway: The window is not memory, it is what gets re-read every single turn — so curate the pile: put the task first and the question last, never bury the line that matters in the middle, and start a fresh chat with a short summary instead of dragging a long thread.
